candidates.name: Sponza Palace
candidates.content: Gothic Renaissance palace, one of the few buildings that has maintained its form from before the catastrophic 1667 earthquake. Hosts historic archives. Memorial room of defenders.

candidates.name: Big Onofrio's Fountain
candidates.content: In the western (Pile) entrance of the old town, The fountain stairs are nowadays a favourite meeting place for local youth and where both the tourists and pigeons take rest and refresh themselves with cool water.

candidates.name: Roland's Column
candidates.content: A slender stone flag staff of the legendary knight. Also known as Orlando's Column. Ever since its foundation in 1950, the Dubrovnik Summer Festival is opened by raising a flag carrying the city's motto Libertus on Orlando's staff

candidates.name: Bell Tower
candidates.content: On top of the tower are the famous 'Zelenci' (The Green Ones), bronze statues which strike the gigantic bell every hour. They have been replaced with copies and the originals are in the atrium of the Sponza Palace.

candidates.name: Rector's Palace
candidates.content: The former palace of the Major Council houses a museum dedicated to the city's history.

candidates.name: Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
candidates.content: This impressive building is in the Poljana Marin Držić. Supposedly, the original church was built with money donated by Richard the Lionhearted who survived shipwreck on his way home from the Third Crusade. The current Roman Baroq

candidates.name: Church of St. Ignatius and the Jesuit College
candidates.hours: Mass held in English daily at 11:00 in the summer
candidates.content: Ornate Jesuit church, approached via a romantic baroque staircase modelled on the Spanish Steps in Rome (1738). Built between 1667 and 1725 by architect Ignazzio Pozzo, and like most Jesuit churches of the period was modelled on t

candidates.name: Dominican Monastery
candidates.content: This is an exceptionally valuable historic complex, which, besides its religious purpose, also represents the important artistic treasury of ancient Dubrovnik.

candidates.name: Synagogue and Jewish Museum
candidates.content: This synagogue built by Sephardic Jews is supposed to be the second-oldest still in use synagogue in Europe today. A permanent Jewish community here was founded at the end of the 15th century following the expulsions from Portugal

candidates.name: Maritime Museum
candidates.content: Considering how vital sailing and shipbuilding were to the growth of the Dubrovnik Republic, this is one of the city’s most important museums.

candidates.name: Pile Gate
candidates.content: A convenient starting place for a stroll through the Old Town.

candidates.name: Fort Lovrijenac
candidates.price: €15, or free with City Walls ticket
candidates.content: The monumental fort rises above 37 m high rock. It was an essential fortification for defence of the city from both ground and sea attacks. In order to prevent mutiny by the commander of the fortress, the walls facing the city are

candidates.name: Franciscan Monastery
candidates.content: This beautiful monastery with Baroque Church, houses a Romanesque cloister and the third oldest pharmacy in the world.

candidates.name: Church of Saint Blaise
candidates.content: Baroque Church dedicated to the city's patron saint.

candidates.name: Dubrovnik Natural History Museum
candidates.content: The collection of 100 year-old taxidermy specimens dates back to 1872 and may not appeal to everyone.

candidates.name: Serbian Orthodox Church and Museum of Icons
candidates.content: Built from 1865-1877, stands behind impressive wrought iron gates. Houses a number of icons, mainly Byzantine and Cretan. Museum next to church has extensive icon collection.

candidates.name: The Ethnographic Museum
candidates.content: Built in 1590, this is a fascinating building, and the exhibits showcase the economic, cultural and spiritual development of Dubrovnik. The folk costumes and textiles give the best flavour of the region where folk culture is still

candidates.name: Bukovac House
candidates.content: Includes works by Vlaho Bukovac (1855-1922), one of the most famous modern Croatian painters. Part of the house is devoted to exhibitions of works by young artists.

candidates.name: Franciscan Monastery Museum
candidates.content: Houses artifacts from one of the world's oldest pharmacies.

candidates.name: Dominican Monastery Museum
candidates.content: Paintings and artifacts from Dubrovnik's past.

candidates.name: The Rector's Palace Museum
candidates.content: Artifacts, paintings and furniture dating from the time of the Dubrovnik Republic.

candidates.name: The Treasury of Cathedral
candidates.content: The Treasury has 138 reliquaries which are carried around the city during the Feast of St Blaise.

candidates.name: War Photo Limited
candidates.hours: Apr Oct: daily 10:00-17:00; May-Sep: daily 10:00-22:00; last admission one hour before closing; Nov-Mar closed
candidates.content: An exhibition centre of war and conflict photography. Exhibits change during the season. Stunning images by world-renowned photo journalists.

candidates.name: Lapad Beach
candidates.content: A car-free, sandy beach area on the Lapad Peninsula, approximately 3.5 km from the old town, where you can relax in the shade of the numerous trees. At the end of a long pedestrianised street full of café bars and restaurants you

candidates.name: Banje Beach
candidates.content: A well-located pebble beach. There's a concessioned part with an entrance fee, but also a public part which is always livelier and more relaxed. Great way to beat the heat in the middle of the town. Amazing view of the city walls,

candidates.name: Lazareti
candidates.content: Old quarantine hospital serves as a cultural centre for concerts, exhibitions, workshops, theater, film, night clubs and literature. The concert hall/bar is a very cozy place with a decent sound system. Gallery Galeriya Tutunplok

candidates.name: Dubrovnik Summer Festival
candidates.content: Music and theatre festival held since 1949 from 10 July to 25 August. Famous nationwide for its exquisite selection of drama, plays and concert of chamber music with more than 2,000 artists from 30 countries during 47 days of fest

candidates.name: Cliff Jumping @ Cafe Buža
candidates.content: See listing for Cafe Buža in the Drinks section.

candidates.name: Dubrovnik Cable Car
candidates.content: The original cable car was bombed during the conflicts and closed in 1991. It reopened to the public for the first time on 10 July 2010. The view of the Old City will rival that found on any postcard. There is a small shop at the

candidates.name: imad hotel
candidates.content: Swim in the Adriatic Sea below the old wall. In the harbour of the old town, go all around (right) along the wall, beyond the aquarium and there is a pier and some rocks where you can cool down on a hot summer day. Avoid stepping

candidates.name: Cafe Buža
candidates.content: The tables and chairs are set out on the side of the cliff and the beers are served in bottles and plastic cups. You can sunbathe on the rocks or do some cliff-diving but do watch for rocks below. This is lovely in the evening, wh

candidates.name: Banje Beach Club
candidates.content: Beach club, bar and Med-style restaurant by day, at night you can party in the nightclub. Great view, various kinds of music, popular DJs and beautiful atmosphere.

candidates.name: Casablanca
candidates.content: Look for flashing red and blue lights. This is an interesting, slightly bizarre bar with seating outside on the city stairs, techno music, and may have erotic dancing.

candidates.name: D'vino Wine Bar
candidates.content: A selection of over 100 fine domestic and imported wine available by the glass, bottle, and in tasting servings. Largest selection of wines by the glass in Dubrovnik with a very intimate, romantic atmosphere, which is a change of

candidates.name: Troubadour
candidates.content: A popular bar/café which comes alive at night with daily live music, usually jazz. Can be very expensive, so you often see people sitting on nearby steps enjoying the music with drinks bought from the nearby Konzum supermarket.

candidates.name: Beer Factory
candidates.content: Despite its sterile sounding name, this place has a lovely courtyard out the back. Its real draw however is that it is possibly one of the cheapest places to get a beer in the old town. Some reasonably priced snacks are also avail

candidates.name: Klub Orlando
candidates.content: Dingy club, predominantly metal but seems to cater for anything deemed alternative. Cheap drink prices with occasional international touring acts, definitely in the minority as a tourist here.

candidates.name: NoneNina
candidates.content: Chill music fills this lounge bar at night, making it a great place to unwind after a full day of sightseeing.

candidates.name: Culture Club Revelin
candidates.content: Dubrovnik's liveliest night spot, techno and other styles.

candidates.name: Lazareti
candidates.content: House and techno music.

candidates.name: Pizzeria La Luna
candidates.content: Large portions. Really good pizza with fresh ingredients. Only pizza is served before 17:00, for pasta or other dishes come later. 2Good pizza, friendly staff but service can be slow.

candidates.name: Barba
candidates.content: Great sea street food, big portions, nice and friendly staff. Even it is full inside, you can order for take away, sit on the steps in front of the restaurant and eat, while looking at the streets of Kings Landing.

candidates.name: Lady Pi-Pi
candidates.content: Worth the climb for magnificent views over the old town from the restaurants' terrace and presumably taking its name from an ancient water feature just outside the restaurant (not for the prudish). Grilled fish with vegetables €15

candidates.name: Konoba Tabak
candidates.content: Great food if you want to have a real taste of fresh fish & local food. A hang-out for the locals.

candidates.name: Domino Steak House
candidates.content: One of the best for a variety of ways of serving steak. Also serves traditional Dalmatian fare.

candidates.name: Marco Polo
candidates.content: Good traditional food served in a small outdoor courtyard. Really nice restaurant with different types of food.

candidates.name: Lokanda Peskarija
candidates.content: Temporarily closed as of May 2022. Traditional Dalmatian appetizers and meals, you get your meal in a large black fisherman's style pot.

candidates.name: Pizzeria Tabasco
candidates.content: Decent and hearty pizza. Service is excellent and very sincere. Situated underneath the cable car system boarding point just near the walls of the old town.

candidates.name: Mea Culpa
candidates.content: One of the best pizzerias on what is becoming a 'pizza street'. Go for pizza or a coffee and brandy and exchange banter with the staff.

candidates.name: Pizzeria Scala
candidates.price: €6 for a normal 30 cm pizza; €7-11 for delicious Mexican food/specialities
candidates.content: A very nice pizzeria between Lapad and Babin Kuk with good pizza and very good Mexican food/specialities.

candidates.name: Dubravka 1836
candidates.content: Variety of pizzas, meat and seafood dishes, quality domestic and foreign wines, cocktails, homemade ice cream and desserts.

candidates.name: Taj Mahal
candidates.content: Offers a variety of Bosnian and Eastern cuisine such as Cevapcici u lepinji, baklava and tufahi. The wait can be quite long, and vegetarian options are often sold out.
